title: Sign analysis — how one variable moves when another changes

questions.stem: Pressure is P = F ÷ A. If the force F stays the same and the area A increases, the pressure
questions.explanation: Rule 2. A is under the bar, so it moves the result the opposite way. Spread the same force over more area and the pressure drops — that is why a wide footing sinks less than a narrow one.

questions.stem: In R = V ÷ I, if V increases and I decreases at the same time, then R
questions.explanation: Both changes push the same way here. A bigger numerator raises R, and a smaller denominator also raises R. When two changes agree you get a definite answer.

questions.stem: In R = V ÷ I, if V increases and I also increases, then R
choices: cannot be determined without the amounts
questions.explanation: The two effects fight each other. A bigger V pushes R up, a bigger I pushes R down, and without knowing how much each changed you cannot say which wins. Recognising the indeterminate case is part of the skill — do not force an answer.

questions.stem: A relationship chain: when A increases, B decreases. When B decreases, C decreases. If A increases, then C
questions.explanation: Rule 4. Follow each arrow in order: A ↑ → B ↓ → C ↓. One reversal, so the end of the chain moves opposite to the start.

questions.stem: A relationship chain: when A increases, B decreases. When B decreases, C increases. If A increases, then C
questions.explanation: Rule 4 again. A ↑ → B ↓ → C ↑. Two reversals cancel out and put you back where you started.

questions.stem: The product of five negative numbers is
choices: positive or negative depending on size
questions.explanation: Rule 4. Count the negatives. Five is odd, so the result is negative. Size never affects the sign.
Three negative factors — an odd count — so the answer is negative. The magnitude is 3 × 2 × 4 × 1 = 24, giving −24.

questions.stem: Time equals distance divided by speed. If the distance is fixed and the speed increases, the trip time
questions.explanation: Rule 2. Speed sits under the bar, so raising it lowers the time. The sanity check is common sense: drive faster, arrive sooner.

questions.stem: A crew has a fixed materials budget. Total cost is the number of fittings times the price per fitting. If the price per fitting rises, the number they can buy
questions.explanation: Rule 3. The total is held constant, so the two factors trade off. Price up, quantity down.

questions.stem: Friction loss in a pipe run increases with length and decreases with diameter. A run is made both longer and larger in diameter. The friction loss
choices: cannot be determined from what is given
questions.explanation: The two changes work against each other, and no amounts are given, so there is no single answer. On a real test this choice is correct far more often than people expect — when the arrows conflict, say so.

questions.explanation: Work the sign rule backwards. For the quotient to be negative with a positive denominator, the numerator has to be negative.

questions.stem: Work equals force times distance. If the work stays the same and the force is doubled, the distance is
questions.explanation: Rule 3. With the product fixed, doubling one factor halves the other. This is exactly the trade every lever, ramp and pulley makes.

questions.stem: The mechanical advantage of a lever is the effort arm divided by the load arm. If the load arm gets longer while the effort arm stays the same, the effort needed to lift the load
questions.explanation: Two steps. A longer load arm is a bigger denominator, so mechanical advantage falls (rule 2). Less mechanical advantage means more effort for the same load — that is why you move the fulcrum toward the load, not away from it.
